newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian state keen to privatise power distribution.
newsitem.headline: Indian state keen to privatise power distribution.

text.p: India's eastern state of Orissa is keen to privatise power distribution, a senior state government official said on Tuesday.

"The Orissa government is in favour of substantial privatisation of electricity by the end of March 1999," K. B. Verma, the senior civil servant in Orissa's energy department told Reuters in an interview.
"To begin with, separate companies will be formed for four distribution zones in the state and made operational from the next fiscal," he added.
Backed by the World Bank and the United Kingdom's Department for International Development, Orissa began revamping its loss-making state electricity board in 1994.

The reforms took final shape in early 1996 with the passage of the Orissa Electricity Reforms Bill. The bill laid down structural changes to be made in the ailing sector including private participation in electricity generation, supply and distribution.
The reforms also aim to check power theft and ensure prompt collection of bills from consumers.

The state electricity board's transmission and distribution assets were transferred to the newly created state-run Grid Corp of Orissa (GRIDCO). The state's hydro-electric stations were transferred to Orissa Hydro Power Corp.
The state government estimated a cost of $800 million for structural changes, with the World bank expected to provide $350 million, officials said.
Verma said GRIDCO would divest 51 percent of its shares to the private sector and 10 percent to its 30,000 employees by the end of 1998. It will divest the rest of the shares gradually.
"Foreign companies and investors' can participate in competitive bids, but they have to take an Indian partner," said a senior state government official.
State government officials said that tariff collection in the state rose to 950 million rupees ($26.6 million) in July 1997 in comparison to 700 million rupees in the pre-reform month of March 1996.
The goal is to push this figure to the 1.2-1.3 billion rupees per month mark, to meet debt and operational expenses of GRIDCO.

"The state government is in a hurry to ensue that GRIDCO is able to reach that figure," Verma said. "A privatised distribution system can run the entire system efficiently and consumers can get the best service." ($ = 35.7 Indian Rupees)
